meta.name: Break the Code: Three-Leg Duel
meta.blurb: Two hidden three-digit codes, six question cards, three legs of four rounds: crack your opponent's code early to score big.

steps.label: code choice
steps.text: A new leg starts. Secretly write your code for this leg: three different digits from {digit_min} to {digit_max}, in any order (for example 8 2 5). They are sorted smallest first. Any other entry becomes the code 0-1-2.

steps.label: the codes are set

value.calc: sorted([int(ch) for ch in you.entry if ch in '0123456789'])
(you.digits[0] * 100 + you.digits[1] * 10 + you.digits[2]) if (len(you.digits) == code_length and you.digits[0] < you.digits[1] and you.digits[1] < you.digits[2]) else default_code

steps.text: Both codes are set for this leg. Each player has {guesses_per_leg} guesses and all {question_cards} cards available.

steps.label: ask a card
steps.text: Name one card you have not used this leg; it is answered from your opponent's code A < B < C. 1 SUM: A+B+C. 2 EVENS: how many digits are even (0 is even). 3 RANGE: C-A. 4 HIGH: how many digits are {high_digit_threshold} or more. 5 STEPS: how many of the pairs (A,B), (B,C) differ by exactly 1. 6 THREES: how many digits are 0, 3, 6 or 9.

steps.label: the answers

value.calc: int(you.ask_pick) if you.ask_pick in you.offer else int(you.offer[0])
[[int(p.code / 100), int(p.code / 10) % 10, p.code % 10] for p in players]

[[c[0] + c[1] + c[2], count(d % 2 == 0 for d in c), c[2] - c[0], count(d >= high_digit_threshold for d in c), (1 if c[1] - c[0] == 1 else 0) + (1 if c[2] - c[1] == 1 else 0), count(d % 3 == 0 for d in c)] for c in codes]
[card_values[p.seat - 1][you.ask - 1] for p in players if p.seat != you.seat][0]

steps.text: Seat 1 asked card {players[0].ask}: the answer is {players[0].answer}. Seat 2 asked card {players[1].ask}: the answer is {players[1].answer}.

steps.label: guess
steps.text: Answer 'pass', or guess your opponent's code as a three-digit number made of three different digits in any order (for example 825, or 52 for 0-5-2); it is sorted smallest first. Each player has {guesses_per_leg} guesses per leg (your remaining count is shown in your state). A correct guess scores {correct_score_base} minus the leg-round ({leg_round} now) and you are solved for the rest of the leg; a wrong guess costs {wrong_guess_penalty} point and adds 1 to your wrong-guess count. A number whose digits are not all different is a pass and costs nothing.

value.calc: int(you.guess_entry) if you.guess_entry not in ['pass', '', '-'] else 0

(you.digits[0] * 100 + you.digits[1] * 10 + you.digits[2]) if (you.gnum > 0 and you.digits[0] < you.digits[1] and you.digits[1] < you.digits[2] and you.guesses_left > 0 and you.solved == 0) else pass_value
'pass' if you.guess == pass_value else ('correct' if you.guess == sum([p.code for p in players if p.seat != you.seat]) else 'wrong')

steps.label: check the guesses

when.calc: any(p.guess != pass_value for p in players)

steps.text: Guesses (written 100A+10B+C, 0 means a pass): seat 1 {players[0].guess} is {players[0].last_result}; seat 2 {players[1].guess} is {players[1].last_result}. Scores: seat 1 {players[0].score}, seat 2 {players[1].score}.

steps.label: the leg ends
steps.text: The leg is over and both codes are revealed: seat 1 {players[0].code}, seat 2 {players[1].code}. Scores: seat 1 {players[0].score}, seat 2 {players[1].score}.

over.text: Winner: {result}. Final scores: Seat 1 {players[0].score} ({players[0].wrong_count} wrong guesses), Seat 2 {players[1].score} ({players[1].wrong_count} wrong guesses).

rules:
Two players. The match has {legs} legs of {rounds_per_leg} rounds each ({total_rounds} rounds in total). Leg 1 is rounds 1-4, leg 2 is rounds 5-8, leg 3 is rounds 9-12. The leg-round is ((round - 1) mod 4) + 1, so 1, 2, 3 or 4 within each leg. Scores start at {starting_score} and carry across legs.

CODES. A code is three different digits from {digit_min} to {digit_max}, kept smallest first as A < B < C (example: 2-5-8). Codes are written as the number 100A+10B+C, so 2-5-8 is 258 and 0-1-2 is 12.

THE SIX QUESTION CARDS. Each answer is one number computed from the opponent's current code A < B < C.
1 SUM: A + B + C (2-5-8 gives 15).
2 EVENS: how many of the three digits are even, 0 counting as even (2-5-8 gives 2).
3 RANGE: C - A (2-5-8 gives 6).
4 HIGH: how many of the three digits are {high_digit_threshold} or more (2-5-8 gives 2).
5 STEPS: how many of the pairs (A,B) and (B,C) differ by exactly 1: 0, 1 or 2 (3-4-5 gives 2, 2-5-8 gives 0).
6 THREES: how many of the three digits are 0, 3, 6 or 9 (0-3-7 gives 2).

EACH ROUND:
1. Code choice (leg-round 1 only: rounds 1, 5, 9). Both players simultaneously and secretly write a code. Three different digits written in any order are sorted ascending and become that player's code for this leg. Any other entry (repeated digits, wrong count, non-digits, blank) becomes the code 0-1-2. Only the engine knows the codes; you see only your own. Each player's guesses for the leg are set to {guesses_per_leg}, their solved flag to no, and their used cards to none.
2. Ask. Both players simultaneously and secretly name one card number (1-{question_cards}) they have not used in this leg; you are only offered the cards you have not used. If a player names nothing or an invalid card, they are given the lowest-numbered card they have not used this leg. The card becomes used for that player until the leg ends. Each player uses exactly {cards_used_per_leg} different cards per leg; all six are available again at the start of the next leg.
3. Answer. The engine computes each player's card from the opponent's code and announces to both players which card each player asked and the answer.
4. Guess. Both players simultaneously either pass or write a code guess, as a three-digit number (825, or 52 for 0-5-2). A guess of three different digits in any order is sorted ascending. Any other entry counts as a pass. A player with 0 guesses left, or who has already guessed correctly this leg, is not asked and passes. A pass costs nothing. A valid guess uses up 1 of that player's guesses for the leg.
5. Check. Each valid guess is compared with the opponent's code. Correct (all three digits match): the guesser scores {correct_score_base} minus the leg-round, so 4 points in leg-round 1, 3 in leg-round 2, 2 in leg-round 3, 1 in leg-round 4; the guesser is marked solved for the rest of the leg and makes no further guesses that leg. Wrong: the guesser loses {wrong_guess_penalty} point and also gains 1 to their wrong-guess count. Every guess and its result (correct or wrong) is announced to both players. One player guessing correctly does not end the leg for the other player, who may keep asking and guessing.
6. Leg end (leg-round 4 only: rounds 4, 8, 12). Both codes are revealed to both players, and the current scores are announced.
7. End check. After round {total_rounds} the match ends.

WINNING. After round {total_rounds}, the player with the higher total score wins. If the totals are equal, the player with fewer wrong guesses over the whole match wins. If that is also equal, the match is a draw and both share the win.
